items.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I made recordings with a lot of people like Stanley Turrentine and Horace Silver and Frank Foster, Donald Byrd.

ctx.x: Yes. Well see when I first went to New York I didn’t know how to read music. You know I studied very briefly and then I got drafted in the Army. So when I came out of the Army I went to New York to play with Gigi, then I played with Ray Bryant, then Joe Williams. And when I left Joe Williams I took a gig with Mary Lou Williams in the Hickory House. And I worked with her for about a year off and on, then she got sick. So

during that time I decided I was going to stay in New York for a while. So I got hooked up with Duke Pearson and Duke Pearson more or less taught me how to read you know. Because he had a big band. And then he asked me to join his big band. And then he would write out stuff for me and then I started to learn, when I first started to learn how to read. So then I got the gig with Nancy Wilson. Because she had music for everything. And that was beautiful man, you know, that was one of the best jobs I ever had in my…
Let me ask you about that, ‘cause you talked about Horace Silver. First of all the hard bop period is like some of my favorite music. Tell me about how that music feels from the inside out.
